ran: favicon — zchuyot was one of the twelve 'blocked on an asset'. It turns out it carries an asset; the asset is the builder's, and that is measurable rather than assumed.
follows: QA/platform/favicon-mounts-0810/_results.json — that round measured all 24 mounts and found 16 drawing the portal's mark, twelve of them with no icon asset of their own. zchuyot was counted among the twelve.

what_the_twelve_were_blocked_on_actually.claim_tested: the previous round wrote that pointing these mounts at the builder's default .ico would trade the portal's mark for the builder's — stated as a judgement, not measured
what_the_twelve_were_blocked_on_actually.how_measured: SHA-256 of every favicon.* under apps/ (excluding node_modules and .git)
what_the_twelve_were_blocked_on_actually.conclusion: four byte-identical copies across four unrelated Lovable projects, two of them archived. It is the builder's default. The judgement was right, and it is now a measurement.
what_the_twelve_were_blocked_on_actually.not_claimed: the other ten of the twelve were not hashed for this — the scan found no favicon.* in their trees at all, which is a different finding (no asset) from zchuyot's (a borrowed asset).

the_mark_that_was_authored.derived_from: the product's own live tokens in src/index.css — primary 152 45% 32% (#2D7654), emerald-dark 152 50% 22% (#1C543A), secondary/gold 42 85% 55% (#EEB32B); the 135° gradient direction is hero-gradient's
the_mark_that_was_authored.letter: ב — the initial of «בקלות», which is what the navbar actually draws (Navbar.tsx:59, a text wordmark with no graphic mark beside it)
the_mark_that_was_authored.why_a_path_and_not_text: an SVG used as a favicon is loaded as an image, so it fetches no external resource: Rubik would never arrive, and the system fallback is not guaranteed to cover Hebrew on every OS. The letter is drawn as a stroked path.
the_mark_that_was_authored.explicitly_not_used: src/components/AnimatedLogo.tsx draws a ring-and-checkmark mark in the same palette and looks like the obvious source — it is dead code. No file imports it, and the path literal 'M20 30 L27 37 L40 22' does not appear anywhere in the built bundle. A favicon taken from it would have been a mark no visitor has ever seen.

a_defect_this_round_produced_and_caught.what: the first version of favicon.svg did not render at all — broken image at every size
a_defect_this_round_produced_and_caught.cause: its header comment cited the CSS custom properties verbatim (--emerald-dark, --primary). An XML comment may not contain two consecutive hyphens, so the whole document failed to parse.
a_defect_this_round_produced_and_caught.why_it_was_caught: the file served 200 image/svg+xml at the right byte count, and the browser issued the request — every check short of rendering it passed. Only the render showed the break.
a_defect_this_round_produced_and_caught.fixed: the comment now names the tokens without their leading double hyphen, and says why

verified_on_a_real_render.how: vite build, then vite preview on port 4361 (base /zchuyot/), then a real Chromium page load of http://127.0.0.1:4361/zchuyot/
verified_on_a_real_render.not_grep: the check is the resolved href in the live DOM, the request the browser itself issued, and the decoded image
verified_on_a_real_render.browser_actually_requested: http://127.0.0.1:4361/zchuyot/favicon.svg (request #19, no query string — the tab's own fetch)
verified_on_a_real_render.asset_response: 200 image/svg+xml 1328 bytes on the first build; the corrected file is 1658 bytes and was copied into dist and re-served
verified_on_a_real_render.origin_root_favicon_svg: 404 — the fallback production takes is not reachable here
verified_on_a_real_render.decoded: naturalWidth/naturalHeight 64×64 at all four render sizes, img.decode() resolved — i.e. the document parses
verified_on_a_real_render.vite_did_not_double_prefix: dist/index.html carries href="/zchuyot/favicon.svg" exactly as written; Vite left the root-absolute href alone rather than applying base to it
verified_on_a_real_render.bundle_unchanged: index-0ikxyjGB.js before and after — no JS was touched

screenshot.what_it_is: the asset rendered as an at 16/32/64/128 px, inside the running page
screenshot.what_it_is_not: a picture of the tab. A tab icon lives in the browser chrome, not the viewport, and screenshot cannot capture it — the evidence for the tab is the resolved href and the network request.

not_claimed: not deployed. The build was not copied into _deploy/zchuyot-more30, so production still serves the portal's mark for this mount.
nothing was measured about the other eleven mounts this round.
public/favicon.ico (the builder default) was left in place and is simply not declared. Nothing requests it: the browser's .ico fallback goes to the origin, not the mount.
no ICO or PNG was authored, so a client that ignores SVG icons still falls back to the origin.
